title: BackLink
wrapsNative: NavigationStack with NavigationLink: the system back button; the dismiss environment action to go back from code
summary: Going one level up is the back button that NavigationStack adds to every pushed screen. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Push detail screens with NavigationLink or navigationDestination inside a NavigationStack. The back button, its label, the edge swipe and the long-press history are the system's.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a back link in the content of a screen, and do not hide the system back button to replace it with one. To close a sheet use a Cancel or Done button in its toolbar.
api: func navigationTitle(_ title: String) -> some View

states.name: pushed
states.description: The navigation bar shows a back chevron with the title of the previous screen.

states.name: long previous title
states.description: The system shortens the label to "Back" when the title does not fit.

appearance: The system draws the back button in the tint of the navigation stack. monarchTheme sets the tint to the theme's accent, so apply it outside the NavigationStack. The chevron mirrors in a right-to-left layout.
platformNotes: The web BackLink is a link in the page content with a leading arrow, a variant and its own text ("Back to domains"). On iOS the label is the previous screen's navigation title, so name screens well instead of writing a back label. The web's variant has no equivalent: the bar is the system's. Android uses the navigation icon of the top app bar and the system back gesture.
accessibility: System behaviour: the back button is read as the previous screen's title with "Back button".
System behaviour: the VoiceOver escape gesture (a two-finger Z) and the edge swipe go back.
System behaviour: with a hardware keyboard, Command and the left bracket go back.
edgeCases: navigationBarBackButtonHidden(true) also turns off the edge swipe; use it only to guard unsaved changes, with a visible way out.
dismiss() pops the current screen from the stack; in a sheet it closes the sheet.
The root screen of a stack has no back button.

examples.title: Variants

parityExceptions.reason: Decision: web-only, the platform convention applies. there is no BackLink component; going up is the system back button of the navigation stack (iOS) or the top app bar navigation icon (Android). The template draws each link as a ghost button with a leading chevron; the web's default and standalone variants (muted and accent text) are not expressed
parityExceptions.convention: HIG navigation: the system back button of the NavigationStack
